meta.title: Fushi — Language Acquisition
meta.description: Fushi: a free, open-source immersion app for language learning. Tap a word while watching anime, reading, or playing games to look it up, tap again to make an Anki card with the sentence, screenshot and audio. Windows / macOS / Android / iOS.
home.hero.title:
Search, download, play, read,
look up and make cards — all in Fushi
home.hero.copy: Anime and manga search, automatic updates and downloads, video playback, manga and novel reading, audiobook sync, and Galgame text and voice hooks (Windows). Look up unfamiliar words on the spot and turn them into Anki cards with the original sentence, image and audio.
home.acgn.title: What you love is the best textbook.
home.acgn.copy: No need to set aside time to “study”. Watching the shows, reading the books and playing the games you like is the study — look up and save new words on the spot, without stopping or switching apps.

home.sec.anki_copy: Every card carries the place it was born: the sentence, a GIF or screenshot, the original audio. Written through AnkiDroid / AnkiMobile / AnkiConnect, with the built-in Lapis note type creating the deck in one tap.
home.sec.downloads_copy: Search AniList / Nyaa inside the app, grab a whole season in one tap, auto-import to the library and play while downloading; subscriptions follow new episodes automatically. libtorrent built in.

home.method.p1: Download Fushi and follow the onboarding guide.
home.method.p2: Pick material you like — that is the single most important thing. Anime (first choice), visual novels or audiobooks are good places to start. Material varies in difficulty; do not force yourself through something too hard.
home.method.p3: When you hit a word you do not know, tap to look it up and make a card (skip it if the sentence is too hard or you are not in the mood). When a whole passage is unclear, try looking things up — and if it still does not click, that is fine, skip it. Learn to tolerate ambiguity: not understanding is normal, and with enough immersion it starts to make sense on its own.
home.method.p4: Learning is slow accumulation. Choose material you genuinely enjoy — interest always comes first; only what you enjoy will keep you immersing every day.
home.method.tip1: When to startYou do not need a big vocabulary before immersing. 500–1000 words is plenty — or honestly, whenever you feel like starting.
home.method.tip2: Improving listeningOnce you know around 2000–5000 words, try watching anime with subtitles hidden. It does wonders for listening.
home.method.tip3: About subtitlesUse subtitles in the target language — the same language as the video. Early on you can add native-language subtitles as a second track to help, but they are a crutch: drop them as soon as you can. With enough vocabulary, try hiding subtitles altogether.
home.closing.title:
You are already learning.
All you need is the tool.

dl.title: Download Fushi
dl.lead: Pick a platform, install it, and let the in-app onboarding handle the rest. Four platforms, one experience, all free and open source.
dl.linux: There is no prebuilt Linux package yet; please build from source.
dl.guide_p1: The first time Fushi starts it opens the onboarding guide: it asks which features you want, then sets up the recommended dictionary pack, Anki, backup sync and reading fonts step by step. Closed it and want to run it again? Go to Settings → System → Onboarding.
dl.guide_r1_b: Choose the interface language and light/dark theme
dl.guide_r2_b: Untick the modules you do not need; they disappear from the bottom bar
dl.guide_r3_b: Download and import Japanese dictionaries plus Japanese/English pronunciation audio
dl.guide_r4_b: Connect AnkiDroid / AnkiMobile / AnkiConnect and create the Lapis deck in one tap
dl.guide_r5_b: Optional — all of these can be skipped
dl.pack_p1: The pack contains Japanese vocabulary, pitch-accent and frequency dictionaries plus local Japanese / English pronunciation audio, about 9.5 GB. Download and import it right from the “Install recommended pack” step of the guide.
dl.pack_warn_body: The pack goes through the backup-import flow. In the confirmation dialog, “Merge into existing library” only adds the dictionaries and audio and leaves your existing data untouched; “Overwrite whole library” replaces the entire library with the pack.
dl.pack_p2: Learning another language? Skip this step and import any Yomitan / MDX (MDict) / DSL / Migaku dictionary through dictionary management. The languages you can look up depend on the dictionaries you import.
dl.channel_debug_hint: Built automatically after every merge: new features and fixes land here first, untested and possibly unstable.
dl.channel_stable_hint: Tested official releases — recommended for everyday use.
dl.chunk_note: “Download” splits the installer into segments in your browser and pulls them from the Cloudflare mirror and the GitHub edge proxy at the same time, then saves the assembled file; unsupported browsers fall back to a normal download.
dl.chunk_fallback: Segment sources unavailable — use the normal download.
dl.warn_no_manifest: Could not fetch the release manifest (neither source answered); the buttons above take you to the GitHub Releases page to choose manually.

dl.p_windows: Includes Galgame voice mining and desktop text lookup
